answer.quote: A total of 58 hospitalizations occurred during the study in 40 patients (Table 2 ); 26 of them for worsening HF (13 in each group) in 17 patients (11 patients on FCM and 6 on usual care).
answer.population: Hospitalisation counts: safety set. Requested denominators: full analysis set (FAS).
answer.notes: FAS size: “A total of 172 patients with HF were studied and received FCM (n=86) or standard of care (control group, n=86).” However, “All-cause mortality and hospitalization for worsening HF and other cardiovascular reasons were analyzed for the safety set.” Thus, the printed patient counts are not explicitly FAS-specific; pairing them with the requested FAS denominators does not establish FAS hospitalisation risks. The 13 in each group counts hospitalisations, not patients.

answer.notes: Neither the supplied text nor either figure prints arm-specific participant/event counts for hospitalized HF alone. Figure 1D prints canagliflozin versus placebo rates of 5.5 versus 8.7 per 1000 patient-years, HR 0.67 (95% CI: 0.52, 0.87), P = 0.002, cumulative percentage curves, and numbers at risk (initially 5795 and 4347); numbers at risk are not event counts. Figure 2, 'Hospitalized HF' rows, has columns headed 'Patients per 1000 patient-years', ordered Canagliflozin then Placebo: history of HF, 14.1 and 28.1, HR 0.51 (0.33, 0.78), ARD −70.17 (−114.34, −26.00); no history of HF, 4.3 and 5.7, HR 0.79 (0.57, 1.09), ARD −6.93 (−15.09, 1.22). Corresponding P interaction values are 0.47 for HR and 0.01 for ARD. The figure labels ARD (95% CI) per 1000 patient-years. The text also prints recurrent HF hospitalization HR 0.68 (95% CI, 0.47–0.96), without arm-specific counts. Composite outcomes in Figure 1A/B are distinct from hospitalized HF alone.
